rows.what the ink shows: A heavy horizontal cancellation covers the baseline; only short low protrusions and a small raised block near its right end remain. No letter sequence can be separated from the strike.

The cancelled word has a curved rising lead-in and two low dark projections below the long stroke. The cancellation merges the middle and final letter bodies, so distinct u and r outlines cannot be established.

After the closing subscript bar, a dense glyph has a tall triangular upper loop, a lower oval, and a descending right arm. Unlike the separated d and s in (3), these overlapping strokes do not securely distinguish two baseline letters.

The tall stem and upper oval support capital Φ, also visible in the earlier cancelled formula. Several thick cancellation loops cross the lower letters and bars; the subscript cannot be separated securely into |AB|.

A low rounded beginning is followed by flattened connected strokes, a small detached dot, and the tall joined middle strokes; two short acute marks sit above the later e strokes before the low ending. The sequence supports considérées, though the central cursive joins are compressed.
The digit has an oblique left arm joining a horizontal lower bar and a straight right downstroke extending below it. This angular construction is 4, without the two open curved lobes of 3.
